text: The Goldbeter-Koshland model of zero-order ultrasensitivity shows that a single phosphorylation-dephosphorylation cycle can produce a switch-like response with an effective Hill coefficient of roughly 20 to 40, without any cooperative binding. Under what condition does this arise?
choices: When the kinase binds its substrate cooperatively with a Hill coefficient greater than 4
When ligand-bound receptors are rapidly internalized by clathrin-mediated endocytosis
When calcium released from the endoplasmic reticulum activates ryanodine receptors in a feed-forward loop
When both the kinase and the phosphatase are operating near saturation with respect to their substrate (zero-order kinetics)
explanation: Zero-order ultrasensitivity requires that both the forward (kinase) and reverse (phosphatase) enzymes be saturated by their substrate, so that small changes in the kinase-to-phosphatase activity ratio produce a sharply switch-like change in the fraction phosphorylated. Cooperative substrate binding (choice 0) is a separate route to ultrasensitivity that this model specifically does not require. Receptor internalization (choice 1) and calcium-induced calcium release (choice 2) describe receptor trafficking and calcium signaling, respectively, not phosphorylation-cycle ultrasensitivity.
